entries.title: Proverbs 26:1
segments: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honor [is] not becoming for a fool.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:2
segments: As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse without cause shall not come.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:3
segments: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:4
segments: Do not answer a fool according to his foolishness, lest you also be like him.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:5
segments: Answer a fool according to his foolishness, so that he may not be wise in his own eyes.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:6
segments: He who sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off the feet [and] drinks down damage.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:7
segments: The legs of the lame [are] not equal; so [is] a parable in the mouth of fools.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:8
segments: As he who binds a stone in a sling, so [is] he who gives honor to a fool.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:9
segments: [As] a thorn goes up into the hand of a drunkard, so [is] a parable in the mouth of fools.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:10
segments: Great [is] the Former of all, but he who hires a fool [is like] one who hires one passing by.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:11
segments: As a dog returns to its vomit, [so] a fool returns to his folly.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:12
segments: Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? [There is] more hope for a fool than for him.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:13
segments: The lazy one says, [There is] a lion in the way; a lion [is] in the streets.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:14
segments: [As] the door turns upon its hinges, [so does] the lazy man turn upon his bed.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:15
segments: The lazy man hides his hand in [his] bosom; it grieves him to bring it again to his mouth.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:16
segments: The sluggard [is] wiser in his own eyes than seven men who can give a reason.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:17
segments: He who passes by enraging himself over strife not his own [is like] one who takes a dog by the ears,

entries.title: Proverbs 26:18
segments: [or] like a madman who throws firebrands, arrows, and death.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:19
segments: so [is] the man who deceives his neighbor and says, Am I not joking.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:20
segments: Where there is no wood, the fire goes out; and where [there is] no talebearer, the fighting ceases.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:21
segments: [As] coals to burning coals, and wood to fire, so [is] a quarrelsome man to kindle fighting.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:22
segments: The words of a talebearer [are] as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:23
segments: Burning lips and a wicked heart [are like] a broken piece of pottery with silver waste.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:24
segments: He who hates pretends with his lips and stores up deceit within him.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:25
segments: When he makes his voice gracious, do not believe him; for seven hateful things [are] in his heart.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:26
segments: [He whose] hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shown before the congregation.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:27
segments: Whoever digs a pit shall fall into it; and he who rolls a stone, it will return on him.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:28
segments: A lying tongue hates [those] afflicted by it, and a flattering mouth works ruin.
